text:
Sam Carter: Quick question — proposing a 'fuzzy compatibility' layer in the onboarding pipeline. Our current exact-match and hard-threshold gates are rejecting quantized / trimmed variants for tiny, semantically-irrelevant diffs. Thoughts?

Izzy Nguyen: saw this yesterday. emb cos sims often dip 0.01-0.03 after q4 -> get flagged but app-level metrics ok.

Kevin Patel: +1. We should separate signal types: embeddings (cosine drift), generations (n-gram overlap / BLEU-ish), and infra (p50/p95 latency). Different tolerances per signal.

Maria Gomez: also think about nondeterministic outputs — punctuation, capitalization, reordering. Hard equality on string isn't helpful.

Izzy Nguyen: proposal sketch: "tolerance profiles" per workload. Example: relevance profile = {emb_cosine: 0.02, rerank_ndcg_drop: 0.007, latency_p95: +15%}. Safety profile = stricter on toxic classifiers.

Sam Carter: I like profiles. How do we enforce? Fail the gate or flag for manual review?

Kevin Patel: two-stage: (1) soft-fail — mark model as "experimental" and shadow route 1-5% traffic; (2) if soft-fail persists beyond grace window (14 days or N runs) -> hard-fail. Also auto-rollback on consecutive regressions.

Maria Gomez: grace windows need to be configurable by customer and model family. Also need a way to encode allowed perturbations (e.g., ignore punctuation-only diffs).

bench-bot: run 2026-02-12 15:04: command: `./bench/run_onboard.sh --model x-q4 --suite relevance-v2 --samples 500`

```
summary: emb_cosine_mean: 0.982 -> baseline 0.993 (delta -0.011)
ndcg@10: 0.728 -> baseline 0.731 (delta -0.003)
latency_p95: 142ms -> baseline 130ms (+9%)
```

Izzy Nguyen: that is a perfect example — emb delta -0.011 would trigger a hard-fail today but product impact is likely negligible. We should allow per-metric hysteresis and historical variance-aware thresholds.

Kevin Patel: implement as: threshold = baseline - max(static_tol, k * baseline_stddev). k tuned per-profile. That gives adaptive tolerance.

Sam Carter: good. What about golden inputs? We need a curated set that surfaces semantic regressions, not random blobs.

Maria Gomez: I'll maintain a 'golden corpus' with tags: semantic, safety, formatting. Bench harness should run both golden and sampled production traces.

Izzy Nguyen: comparator component: fuzzy matcher that supports token-level normalization, synonym expansion, and embedding-based similarity fallbacks. Falls back to human review if ambiguous.

Kevin Patel: infra notes: keep metrics versioned and recorded in registry. Each model entry stores the baseline snapshot + tolerance profile id + last-pass ts. Rollouts read that metadata.

Sam Carter: Ops requirements: alerting when shadow traffic shows >threshold user-visible regressions. Also an opt-out for teams that want strict gating.

Maria Gomez: action items: Izzy to draft RFC for tolerance profiles and comparator API, Kevin to prototype adaptive threshold logic and registry fields, Maria to assemble golden corpus and bench tags. Target: RFC by next Wed, prototype by end of sprint. :thumbsup:

Sam Carter: thanks — moving this to a follow-up doc. Will attach example comparator pseudocode in the RFC. :eyes:
